correction: v001 over-credited rapid Lee/Grant forward deployment by noticing the regiment's historical Dec-1943 transfer but underweighting the Branch destruction of its access routes by Japanese old-battleship bombardment, Japanese territorial advance, and British demolitions.

fixed_branch_obstacles.historical_Ukhia_landing_route: LOST: Ukhia already Japanese-held by mid-November.
fixed_branch_obstacles.reroute: Incoming 25th Dragoons elements must be diverted toward Chittagong/Feni-side unloading and staging rather than landing south of the main river obstacles.
fixed_branch_obstacles.Karnaphuli: A major mobility barrier for 30-ton Lee/Grant tanks; ferry/bridge capacity, approach roads and engineer time become hard gates.
fixed_branch_obstacles.old_battleship_rotation: Fuso/Yamashiro and Ise/Hyuga conduct rotating heavy shore bombardment. Serious anti-port/fixed-target bombardment begins in the 5-7 Dec window and disrupts port handling, road junctions, approach routes, engineer work and vehicle concentration.
fixed_branch_obstacles.British_demolition: Kalurghat bridge is demolished on 11 Dec after rear guards cross; this closes a major crossing rather than creating a convenient armored withdrawal/commitment route.
fixed_branch_obstacles.air_artillery_pressure: Japanese air/artillery observation further discourages daylight concentration of large, high-silhouette Lee tanks.

working_arrival_and_mobility_band.note: These are event bands, not a reconstructed regimental tank return. Exact squadron shipping/unloading diaries remain required.

combat_role_revised.Dohazari_Sangu_Patiya: No regiment-scale Lee intervention centered. At most a very small packet appears, and zero is entirely plausible.
combat_role_revised.Karnaphuli_Chittagong: The more plausible contact window. Small Lee packets can act as local mobile strongpoints/counterattack guns on usable road segments, but cannot maneuver as a regiment.
combat_role_revised.Feni_post_Chittagong: A substantial surviving portion may withdraw or remain north and become part of the later Feni/Comilla defensive arc.

loss_and_intelligence_gate.technical_intelligence: A captured/abandoned Lee remains plausible but not guaranteed. One recoverable wreck/components is the centered intelligence sensitivity, not a whole captured platoon.
loss_and_intelligence_gate.implication: Bengal can reinforce the Allied-30-ton/75mm-medium-tank warning, but GALVANIC and pre-existing intelligence remain necessary co-inputs.

campaign_effect_expectation.casualties: Small-to-moderate upward correction to Japanese losses in the final Chittagong phase if Lee packets engage.
campaign_effect_expectation.capture_date: Current late-14-Dec/early-15-Dec window is more likely to survive than v001 suggested; Lee tanks may buy hours locally, not days, because their mobility network is being physically destroyed.
campaign_effect_expectation.allied_AFV_loss: Reopen composition and loss class, but do not assume the previous 5-10 total must increase dramatically; some new medium-tank presence substitutes for previously generic AFV accounting.

historical_development_input.lesson: The key Tokyo-level message is not that Britain fielded a regiment-scale armored counteroffensive at Chittagong. It is that 30-ton Allied 75mm tanks are physically present in the India-Burma theater and even a small number are awkward for Japanese 37/47mm defense.
historical_development_input.confidence: MEDIUM, rising to MEDIUM-HIGH only if a wreck or detailed after-action examination is confirmed.
